questions.question: You paste 20,000 tokens of runbooks and style guides into the system prompt. What's the main cost?
options: Every request pays for all of it, and unrelated instructions get mixed up; most of it is irrelevant to any one task
questions.explanation: Skills keep know-how available without being present: descriptions always, bodies only when needed.

questions.question: What's always in the model's context in the lesson's design?
questions.explanation: Level 1 is the catalog. Bodies (level 2) and files (level 3) load on demand.

questions.question: Why does the validator warn on 'description: Helps with documents.'?
options: It doesn't say when to use the skill, and the description is all the model has to decide with
Descriptions must be in YAML blocks
questions.explanation: A useful description states what the skill does and when to use it.

questions.question: A skill folder is named pdf-report but its frontmatter says name: report-pdf. What does the validator say?
options: The name doesn't match its folder
questions.explanation: The folder is the skill's identity; a mismatch causes confusing load and install behaviour.

questions.question: The demo task used ~517 + 762 tokens of skill context. Loading all bodies would have cost about…
questions.explanation: Progressive disclosure saved most of the tokens, and the gap grows with every skill added.

questions.question: How do skills and MCP servers relate?
options: MCP gives an agent capabilities (tools); a skill gives it know-how (how to do a task, possibly with those tools)
questions.explanation: They complement each other: tools to act, skills to know how.
